resolution: D-084 now throws only for mutating Response calls after completion; read accessors, isCommitted() and abort() stay legal after next.run() and in onError.

SSE on TinyHttpd no longer uses startEventStream(): headers are set by NaruServe and the stream is a chunked body written on the pinned worker thread from a NaruServe-owned bounded queue; the SSE thread budget is separate and bounded.
Added a mapping of every TinyHttpd budget with defaults that admit T26 from one loopback address; T26 runs on the defaults.
D-225 now covers header-count and wait-queue-length configuration APIs.
RestApp.create() selects Logcat when android.util.Log is present at runtime and console otherwise; the bootstrap depends on the Logcat module from wave 1; the sample confirms it on device.

D-002 lists the SLF4J, rotating file and Logcat logger modules in wave 1. The Logcat logger uses reflection, so the root build stays SDK-free; it is tested against a fake android.util.Log. D-371 is now an item for the sample.
Added the engine-free ResourceResolver interface (open, length, etag, modified) with the File resolver as the v1 implementation; the SAF resolver is post-v1 (P5).
Added a server-wide default Cache-Control policy for static responses (name and default decided in wave 6).
D-067: the enable policy is in the core; on TinyHttpd, CONNECT is always 501 from the parser and is recorded as a deferred TinyHttpd gap.
Added an item that requires the Kotlin sample to use a SAM route, a nullable accessor, a multipart upload, a WebSocket endpoint and req.service.
gradle.properties sets kotlin.stdlib.default.dependency=false, and a build check allows kotlin-stdlib at runtime only in the Kotlin extension module.
I-009 now covers only the JVM Java examples; the Android-only examples compile in the samples/android build.

Section 3 now depends on section 2. Section 2 is the engine-free router: its handler type is opaque and it returns a typed match result. Route registration (moved from section 2), the dispatcher and the HTTP-level T01-T06 assertions through the in-memory adapter now belong to section 3.
Same resolution as V1-002. The SPI event-stream extension point now models the request thread that keeps writing after the handler returns.

D-404 maps maxConnections 512, maxConnectionsPerAddress 256, maxUpgradedConnections 128, SSE streams 128, and maxWorkers = 64 HTTP plus the SSE limit. maxEventStreams is unused. T26 runs on the defaults.

Each wave now adds its own public API. Wave 3 creates Request/Response/RestApp only with types that already exist, D-392 lists which wave owns each later method, JsonCodec is created in wave 4 (D-182 moved there), and D-089/D-100/D-114/D-136 refer to methods added later. I-014 now only forbids changing signatures added earlier.

Section 7 now depends on section 6, so all waves run in series and edits to docs/api/defaults.md and RestApp never overlap. Added a shutdown participant registry in wave 4 that waves 6 and 7 add to. All TinyHttpd builder limits are mapped in the wave 5 adapter core, and D-210 is consistent with that.

onError, the standard JSON and the access log now apply only to requests that reached the dispatcher. TinyHttpd's fixed pre-dispatch responses (400/414/417/431/501/socket 503) are documented as transport-level exceptions. The adapter installs a TinyHttpd ErrorHandler that renders post-parse engine errors as the standard JSON. The worker-queue 503 was removed from the JSON mapping.

TinyHttpd's strict path rules are now the rule on every adapter (any dot segment, encoded slash, NUL, raw non-ASCII: 400). Adapters pass the raw URI and query (getRequestURI/getQueryString, not getPath), and the rejection cases run on both adapters.

Same resolution as V1-006: all optional logger modules and their main dependencies (slf4j-api 1.7.36, bootstrap to Logcat) are declared in wave 1. The Logcat logger is reflective, so no android.jar is needed.
D-194 now states that an untyped Map round-trips only to JSON-value equality, because the default Gson decodes numbers as Double, matching docs/api/request.md.
The router keeps WebSocket and fallback behaviour behind internal hooks. The 426 and the middleware-on-static and middleware-on-upgrade checks are now end-to-end assertions in waves 6 and 7.
The UploadFile.bytes() in-memory limit is now one of D-239's decisions and is written to multipart.md and defaults.md; D-251 points to it.
Symlinks are detected with java.io only, per path component, against a root canonicalised once per mount. Added a test with a symlinked root.
Last-Modified and the If-Modified-Since comparison use the mtime truncated to whole seconds.
The core's multipart parser now serves every adapter, and TinyHttpd's MultipartReader is not used.
Wave 1 replaces every module-name marker in docs/api. D-230 and D-357 are now verification items.
